items.label: RVNG Intl.

items.label: On Rotation
items.context: Adam Pits helps run Leeds label, event and mix platform On Rotation alongside Chris I’Anson and Lisene. His second album for the imprint imagines a digital environment, extending his progressive vocabulary through techno and ambient passages.
items.dig_sentence: Then browse On Rotation’s catalogue for the surrounding Leeds scene.
items.why_candidate: Strong aged-well progressive selection with album-scale development rather than anonymous DJ utility; the earlier Lisene recommendation is not an artist or release repeat.

items.label: Butter Sessions
items.genre: Acid techno; braindance; progressive electronics; downtempo
items.context: Perth producer Guy Contact made his debut long-player for Butter Sessions, the Melbourne/Naarm label run by Sleep D. Developed largely in bedroom sessions after leaving full-time employment, it combines NORI’s vocals, acid movement and slower trance-like passages into a desert-road-inspired sequence.
items.dig_sentence: Next explore Pretty Girl’s fabric presents selection, which places the NORI collaboration in a broader melodic club setting.
items.why_candidate: Promising bridge between Bliss Inc.-adjacent expansiveness and Khotin-oriented home listening, with enough world-building to support a catalogue discovery.

items.label: Michigander Music
items.context: Detroit producer, DJ and mastering engineer Brian Kage runs Michigander Music, which lists this EP in its catalogue. His original is joined by Type-303 and Josh Wink reinterpretations, creating a dialogue around Detroit strings, piano and acid detail.
items.dig_sentence: Next explore Timeless Times for a broader view of Kage’s album-length Detroit vocabulary.
items.why_candidate: A 2026 option connecting Floorplan’s house/techno border territory with melodic-progressive priorities; Featured potential depends on the original retaining its identity beside the remixes.

items.label: Gudu
items.context: Rome-born Italian producer and DJ Matisa issued this four-tracker through Peggy Gou’s Gudu label. Its night-out narrative includes dedications to family, flowers and romantic feeling, with her first vocal appearance adding a personal thread.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Peace Building EP for an earlier chapter of Matisa’s emotionally framed club music.
items.why_candidate: Affirmative aged-well option for the Morphena & Narciss and progressive-house axis; useful Featured alternative when personality-led uplift is preferable to more acid.

items.label: AD 93
items.genre: Experimental dream pop; ambient pop; electronic songcraft
items.context: New York artist james K brings production and an intimate vocal identity to AD 93’s electronic catalogue. Collaborators include Adam Feingold, Francis Latreille, Patrick Holland, Special Guest DJ, Hank Jackson and Ben Bondy, linking personal songwriting to a wider production community.
items.dig_sentence: Next explore the preceding Hypersoft Lovejinx Junkdream release as a smaller entry point into this album’s world.

items.label: Mexican Summer
items.context: São Paulo musician Sergio Sayeg records as Sessa, continuing his Mexican Summer chapter with this third full-length. Fatherhood shifts its emotional perspective while electric piano, synthesis, wah-wah guitar and primitive drum machines expand his previously guitar-centred arrangements.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Grandeza to hear the more stripped-back starting point of Sessa’s songwriting.
items.why_candidate: Strong recent home contender for Os Tincoãs and Jorge Ben listening, offering an organic counterweight without defaulting to historical-canon recommendations.

items.label: Craigie Knowes
items.genre: Acid house; progressive club electronics; techno
items.context: Carsten Fluck and Lucas Lejeune’s not even noticed return to Craigie Knowes, the Scottish label and DJ partnership based in Perth, following their 2023 debut there. A recurring 303 voice links four tracks built around progression and carefully shaped energy.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Adam Pits’s Synthetic Serenity for a longer-form exploration of related progressive machinery.
items.why_candidate: Recent alternative to the heavily represented Haws/Kalahari circuit; conditional promotion depends on whether the four-track arc exceeds competent DJ utility.

items.context: Narciss joins Running Back founder Gerd Janson for the inaugural release in the label’s Studio Sessions series. Their intergenerational studio encounter pairs Italo-coloured hooks and analogue melodies with a Coloray vocal collaboration.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Eoin DJ’s Ode To Beachball EP for a more Balearic route into melodic club euphoria.

items.label: Wisdom Teeth
items.genre: Mutant tech house; dubby house; experimental club
items.context: London producer Facta co-runs Wisdom Teeth with K-LONE; this two-track release returned him to the dancefloor after Blush. Modulating FM bass and reversed synthesis distinguish its shifting structures from straightforward nostalgic tech-house revival.
items.dig_sentence: Then browse Facta’s catalogue to trace the movement between club records and more reflective work.
items.why_candidate: Useful left turn from progressive house with a direct K-LONE connection; reserve status reflects the need to test captivation beyond its concise functional format.

items.label: Lillerne Tapes
items.context: Madelyn Byrd’s Slowfoam and Tim Bomberg’s Neilll collaborated across an ocean on this EP for cassette imprint Lillerne Tapes, issued in an edition of 75. Warm melodic cushioning and sharper interruptions frame connection as both its working method and subject.
items.dig_sentence: Next play Roméo Poirier’s Surfaces for another intimate investigation of tactile electronic space.
items.why_candidate: Direct response to recent Slowfoam additions without repeating the saved Transcorporeal Portal; More listening candidate with promotion potential if the collaboration proves sufficiently distinct.

items.label: Casa Voyager
items.context: Driss Bennis presents his OCB identity through Casablanca-based label Casa Voyager. This compact eight-track electronic album includes Slikk Tim and 95 Steps, using its collaborative cast and tightly framed rhythm pieces as a counterweight to more continuously euphoric progressive records.
items.why_candidate: Electro-led diversification with melodic and rhythmic eccentricity that could connect with Aphex Twin; audition before promotion because independent editorial corroboration was not captured.

items.label: Music From Memory
items.context: Gaussian Curve unites Gigi Masin, Jonny Nash and Marco Sterk on Music From Memory. Their second album grew from rehearsals into spacious recording sessions where piano, guitar, synthesis, drum machines and occasional trumpet retain distinct identities within a shared atmosphere.
items.dig_sentence: Then browse Gaussian Curve’s artist shop for the trio’s companion recordings.
items.why_candidate: Aged-well alternative to the trio’s better-known debut, fitting Air and Domenique Dumont interests; retain as More listening pending ownership and discovery-value checks.
